Around October 30/31 I started to notice similar muscle tightness and "incomplete" breaths, provoking a significant anxiety response again. I did my best to self-manage with the albuterol, muscle stretching, and meditation. On November 1 I was seen by an urgent care center, with a follow-up chest x-ray on November 3. The x-ray was described to me as "normal, with some bronchitis" and I was advised to continue using the albuterol. I spoke with my PCP, on November 8, who recommended I switch from the albuterol to Flovent (fluticasone) since albuterol can increase heart rate and perceived anxiety. He was placed on diltiazem gtt with heart rates decreasing to the 70s and was admitted to the ICU. January 4, 2021 pain, numbness and now weakness have persisted all weekend, appointment with Neurologist scheduled for Tuesday January 5, 2021. January 5, 2021, appointment with Neurologist, suspecting Parsonage-Turner Syndrome.   Parsonage Turner syndrome (PTS) is characterized by the sudden onset of shoulder and upper arm pain followed by progressive (worsening over time) weakness and/or atrophy of the affected area. The pain is felt along the path of one or more nerves and often has no obvious physical cause. The network of nerves involved in this syndrome is called the brachial plexus and it controls movement and sensation in the shoulders and arms. The cause is still unknown (idiopathic). However, researchers believe that most cases are due to an autoimmune response following exposure to an illness or environmental factor. Suspected triggers include viral and bacterial infections, surgery, vaccinations, injury, childbirth, strenuous exercise, certain medical procedures, and various health conditions. Treatment is symptomatic and may include pain relievers, corticosteroids and physical therapy.[1][2] January 6, 2021- MRI of left shoulder completed January 8 2021- Follow up of MRI with neurologist. No abnormalities seen on MRI, ruled out any other tumors, or anatomical issues causing pain. Diagnosis Parsonage-Turner Syndrome. Increased dosages of current medications and added another to control nerve pain.  January 9, 2021- pain seems to be lessening, numbness and weakness continues January 10, 2021- significant pain returned, numbness and weakness continues. I stayed at the hospital for 1 week because they were trying to control my blood pressure and pulse when I would stand up, still till this day I cannot walk/run my 5 miles. Shortly after 1st Moderna shot on Mar 2 2021 I had what I thought was an asthma exacerbation. When breathing did not improve with previously prescribed rescue inhaler and daily oral medication, I saw my primary on Mar 26, 2021.  My primary gave me a  nebulizer treatment, prescribed a z-pack and renewed my Albuteral rescue inhaler. I got no relief from those interventions. On Mar 30, 2021 I had my 2nd Moderna vaccination. I walk daily, usually fast paced with moderate-high exertion, but while having difficulty breathing I  walked slowly with light exertion. On Apr 2nd I was on my walk, short of breath, when I experienced pain in my left chest which moved into my left arm. My left arm was tingling then numb. I stopped and rested until the pain went away, maybe 3-4 minutes. I continued walking  back to the car. My arm remained tingling and numb during that time and for about 30 minutes.  I never felt the same level of pain that I did on April 2nd, but I continued to have shortness of breath, felt twinges/pinches and sometime a quick stab in my left chest. I also had some tightness/pressure in my left neck/throat. My blood pressure was also higher than normal for me. I have had a couple of asthma attacks in my life, but my asthma has been well-controlled and any breathing issues were always able to be resolved with my acute inhaler and a Nebulizer treatment. I had never had chest pain. I saw my primary at a first available appointment who set me up with appointments for pulmonary and cardiology. During this period I also was prescribed additional medications; 1 baby aspirin/day; Symbicort; Metoprolol; nitro (if needed for chest pain). My breathing got worse with the Metoproplol after 5 days and I was given Amlodipine instead. My breathing got easier with the change in medication. I found that lying down on my side helped my breathing. I have not been wakened by not being able to breathe during sleep and feel good first thing in the morning. Once I start moving around in the morning I feel shortness of breath during normal activity. Some days are  improved, some days aren't as good. I have been avoiding even moderate exertion so I don't know if I would have chest pain like I experienced on Apr 2nd again. In addition to the shortness of breath I still feel a twinge/pinch in my left chest and a tightness/pressure on my left neck/throat area. My cardio cath Left/Right was performed Jun 14, 2021. There was no sign of any issues with my heart and no sign of pulmonary hypertension. As of this submission on  Jun 15, 2021, I am grateful that there are no problems or concerns with my heart or lungs. I'll follow my doctor's orders to increase exercise and will have a Pulmonary Function Test in July. I was a person who went from being able to walk 3 miles at a fast pace with 100 foot elevation changes within 1/4 mile to having difficulty walking from my kitchen to the bathroom in a matter of weeks. The only anomaly in that time frame was my 2 Moderna vaccine shots. I'm submitting this because I feel you should know and because I am concerned with what I should do if a booster is required in the future.

ER doc told me to see my dr in the morning and they would set me up for an echogram and a cardiologist.  I went to my dr Dec 7 at 11:15am and was having more squeezing and not feeling good.  Doctor did another EKG because she didn't like how I looked and again it confirmed pericardititis again.  She perscribed me colchicine tablet 2 x day.  I have since had two additional days of chest squeezing feeling.  Once on December 12 lasting about 8 hours and again December 16 not quite as bad as first days but squeezing and uncomfortableness. I have not yet seen a cardiologist

symptom_text: 15 mins post-vaccination: patient developed superficial numbness on skin R side of face, eyes, nose, mouth & chin. Sensation spread to R side forehead, mouth, tongue & back of throat. Became apprehensive and at first was alert & oriented but then had difficulty answering questions & speaking.  BP declined to 100/50, O2 decreased to 90%, lungs had decreased breath sounds with no wheezes.  Epipen administered at 1000. VS stabilized: BP 130/60, P 100, R18, O2 sat returned to 98%. Pt was apprehensive, drowsy, confused and had difficulty answering questions.  Transport to ER via EMS. Mental status deteriorated en route, 50mg diphenhydramine administered. Abnormal clenching/tension of hands & lower extremities. Arrived at ER 1040; did not respond to triage nurse. Pulse 114.  EKG scan performed on arrival. CMP, CBC, HCG drawn. Dexamethasone 10mg & lorazepam 1mg administered. EKG, tox screen & MRI performed; all unremarkable. Patient became able to ambulate and use bathroom with minimal assistance. Became awake and oriented and could answer questions, but felt groggy. Discharged at 1446. ER visit 3 hours.

Symptoms worsened and she re-presented to ED where she was admitted and diagnosed with UTI and colitis. She was started on ciprofloxacin. She denied having had any dysuria or diarrhea. Patient's son says that at 0130 on 4/19 his mother was using both sides of her extremities equally. She had been complaining of headache and leg pain, but by 0130 on 4/19 family did not notice any other obvious changes in patient's movements or behavior. However, at 0730 on 4/19 nurses noticed that patient was unable to move her L arm or leg. She had a CT scan done, which revealed multiple intraparenchymal hemorrhages bilaterally as well as subarachnoid hemorrhage with midline shift. The transferring physician told me that patient had not been on any anticoagulation. Patient and her family deny any history of falls or trauma, denied family history of coagulopathies, and use of blood thinners (including aspirin). No records, labs, or inpatient med list was sent with patient upon transfer. Family says that patient had her first Moderna COVID19 vaccine 3 weeks ago and was due for her second vaccine on 4/23. Labs on admit here are significant for leukocytosis with WBC of 21.9, Hgb of 12.1, platelets of 306, sodium of 140, potassium of 3.1, Bicarb of 22, creatinine of 0.7, glucose of 126, magnesium of 1.8, INR of 1.2. Patient is normotensive, afebrile, and satting well on room air.  Angiogram showed multiple cortical vein thromboses.  Will send hypercoagulable work up, HIT antibody given COVID vaccine 3 weeks ago (Moderna).

The platelet count was 64 x 10*9/L on the day after the vaccination and subsequently dropped to 27 x 10*9/L the following day. The discussion included: vaccination associated ITP was a rare phenomenon. ITP after COVID19 vaccination was relatively a new occurrence, and the management and outcomes of these cases were not well published in medical literature. This report described case of severe ITP that occurred following vaccination and provided insights into the treatment and outcome for ITP secondary to covid-19 vaccination. The patient responded well to treatment with corticosteroids Â± IVIG and if the treatment were not effective, and the platelet count remained very low, it would then be reasonable to escalate therapy to include a thrombopoietic agent and potentially vinca alkaloids depending upon response. Avoiding rituximab from initial treatment would be appropriate since the response to rituximab would take up to 6Â–8 weeks; furthermore, the response to COVID-19 vaccine may be impaired by rituximab. It remains uncertain whether post COVID-19 vaccination ITP cases will prove to be self-limiting or persist and lead to chronic ITP and also unclear if the ITP is secondary to the vaccination or primary ITP that was coincident with the vaccine. The clinical manifestation and the positive response to treatment akin to ITP, such as with corticosteroids Â± IVIG, suggest an antibody-mediated platelet destruction. ITP has been previously reported with different types of vaccines including hepatitis B virus (HBV) human papilloma virus (HPV) varicella zoster, haemophilus infuenza, polio, pneumococcus, Diphtheria-tetanus-acellularpertussis (DTap) and measles-mumps rubella (MMR). Proposed mechanisms include molecular mimicry and antibody generation to adjuvants/additives included in the vaccine composition which can lead to generation of autoantibodies that cause platelet destruction and inhibit platelet production. Data also show that post-vaccination ITP ranges in severity from mild to moderate to severe and is highly responsive to IVIG treatment. Literature review shows conflicting data as some studies show evidence of ITP reactivation when exposed to the same vaccine while others do not demonstrate the ITP reactivation when the vaccine is repeated. Many authors believe that ITP is not an absolute contraindication for vaccination given a much higher rate of ITP linked with natural infection as compared to vaccination however recommend to avoid vaccination during active ITP flare. The conclusion included: As mass vaccination progresses, more data should be collected to establish a cause-effect relationship of COVID-19 vaccination and associated ITP so that guidelines could be formulated for safe administration for COVID-19 vaccination. This could be done by outlining possible contraindications and potential treatment measures for ITP so as to prevent fatal outcomes. Additionally, more research may be needed to make changes in vaccine composition to prevent thrombocytopenia. One consideration could be to monitor patients with history of ITP for an antibody response and reserving the second dose of the vaccine for those without an adequate response. Until there is further development of appropriate guidelines, physicians should discuss these risks and benefits. The action taken with covid-19 vaccine ad26.cov2.s was not applicable. I got the vaccine on 6:30 PM of 10/11/2024 and think I had palpitations from 5:00 AM - 8:00 AM 10/12/2024. I wear an Watch and started getting notifications that my bpm was elevated in my resting state. Normally my resting bpm is in the 80s (lower when I sleep). For most of yesterday, 10/12/2024, it was in the 110s and 120s (even while sleeping). I was all getting dizzy standing up and down. When I stood up yesterday, my bpm would drop to the 40s. This morning, I'm down, to the 90s, and not having issues standing up. I'm mostly just back to my achiness symptoms. (Which were happening throughout). MY REASON FOR REPORTING THIS IS JUST BECAUSE every time I tried to look up common side effects, elevated bpm never showed up. My results when I searched "elevated bpm side effectrs of covid vaccine" and "how long does elevated bpm after coivd vaccine last" were ALWAYS ver ALARMING alarming case reports,  articles or pages on hospital sites that said arrhythmias, myocarditis, and POTS could be RARE, BUT SERIOUS LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCES that affect a very small number of people. I almost when to Urgent Care or the ER. Instead, I called my pharmacist and she said elevated bpm happens to people. She calmed me down and said to follow up with a doctor if it lasted 2-3 days. I also came across a lot of anecdotal forums with people describing similar symptom, and that made me feel better. But what I don't understand is why  the CDC and agency fact sheets do not list elevated bpm as a COMMON side effect of the vaccines. Again, any simple. IS this scaring other people? The pharmacist was very helpful and triaged my concern. Is this a new phenomena? (Was it maybe compounded by the tylenol?). Also, this was the first time I got my flu shot at the same time. I got both on Friday. Will this be listed a new side effect to not worry too much about unless it persists? I'm still not back to normal, and am worried. I may follow up with a doctor if my bpm stays elevated (though, it's much lower now). I'm just surprised this side effect is not described at all by common fact sheets meant to prepare the public for what they might experience.

I felt well enough at the one-week mark to go for a ride on my motorcycle but I didn't last long as the shoulder pain really flared up. symptom_text: She got her J & J vaccine around 4:30 on April 7th ,2021.  She was feeling fine up until around 10:00 that night when she began to have some of the regular side effects in addition to some unusual ones that were more concerning.  She had chills was feverish and nauseous with flu like symptoms of her body aching.  However, at around 10:30 that night she reported having difficulty breathing and having chest pains with pain when she would take breaths. She noticeably was taking very small but frequent breaths due to the pain. She described a pressure on her chest as if there was a bowling ball sitting on top of her chest. She was crying from the pain and her difficulty breathing. She also reported that her throat felt like it was smaller/ constricted.    At that time, she was given Acetaminophen and later around 12:00 she was given Benadryl.  When she went to bed that night, she was in pain but she also reported that her heart was racing and her resting pulse at the time was 110 bpm. She had the flu like symptoms into Thursday evening but by Friday she looked a lot better except for her difficulty breathing with complaints of chest pain when she breaths with continued pressure on her chest.  She rested in bed for most of Friday and on Saturday she got dressed in the afternoon and took a walk around half a mile at which time she was exhausted and felt out of breath.  When she walked back from her destination about a half mile, she needed to rest in bed to recuperate.  The pain while breathing lasted into Sunday. Monday morning, she attempted to run and became winded from running a short distance of Â¼ of the block and could not catch her breath having difficulty breathing and throwing up with a lot of subsequent chest pain that day. She was taken to the doctor by 10:00 that morning to run lab tests and get an examination.  She is slowly getting better and taking it easy but Tuesday she still had some pain and by Thursday she is reporting that while the chest pain is still there it is more of a discomfort that she feels when breathing as compared to pain.  She continues to report the discomfort when breathing till today 4/16/21 and is still limiting her physical activity but going about her daily routine.

He was completely coherent by this point and said he had no other symptoms. 911 was called upon my immediate entrance to the scene by the front end manager. Common side effects of vaccination including low grade fever, chills/hotflashes, and intense body/bone aches began approximately 9/15 at 2300.  I awoke at 0600 noting my heart rate to be at 122 bpm via radial manual pulse, my smart watch, and pulse oximetry; after walking short distance to kitchen, my heart rate was then 140 bpm. I figured maybe I just need to take my metoprolol. I do have a history of tachycardia for unknown reasons at this time but my rates have been controlled between 80-90 or less... even with activity usually my heart rate stays below 120 bpm now. At that time, I took my metoprolol; the day before I had taken it at approximately the same time given that is when I had gotten up for work. I was able to fall back asleep within an hour. I woke up again approximately 120 bpm... I could feel instantly that my heart rate still felt elevated. I checked my watch and pulse oximetry again to find my heart rate was still around 120 bpm just having woke up, still laying in bed. This is quite uncommon for me given my rates have been well-controlled for months now. I ended up discussing with employee health at my workplace who urged me to seek care so I went to the Urgent Care. Heart rate documented at 127 bpm and other vital signs within normal limits. EKG was completed showing sinus tachycardia at 113 bpm. End result was to increase metoprolol dosage until symptoms passed; if they did not improve, pursue ER care. Taking an additional 25 mg on top of my 50 mg ER metoprolol brought my heart rate down for the remainder of the day to 90-100... still elevated from my normal but tolerable. The following day as common symptoms improved so did my heart rate.   I understand this reaction is likely due to my bodies response to creating antibodies; however,  elevated heart rate was not listed as possible side effect which is drastically important for someone like me who has these issues being managed chronically. Expecting tachycardia as a  response would have changed possibly which vaccine I received as well as my medical treatment. Provider at Urgent Care stated that none of their provider's were aware of tachycardia as a common reaction.

She relates the hives worsened on Sunday, April 18 essentially from "head to toe" although not actually involving her face.  She also related new accompanying symptoms including diffuse arthralgias, stiffness and swollen painful muscles and joints.  This was throughout her entire body and somewhat of a migratory nature involving all of her major joints including the hands, wrists, shoulders, feet, ankles, knees and hips.  She states that because of the severity of symptoms she had an urgent care appointment on Sunday, April 18 and felt to have a exacerbation of urticaria for which she was prescribed montelukast, loratadine cimetidine and a Solu-Medrol Dosepak.  She states she was unable to fill the Solu-Medrol Dosepak initially but took the other medications without relief and then presented to the emergency room here at Hospital on Monday, April 19 where she had an evaluation which was largely unremarkable other than laboratory testing with a nonspecific elevation in inflammatory markers including a CRP of 5.7, ESR 34 and white blood count 15.92. She was discharged home and ended up filling the Solu-Medrol Dosepak which she took and noted some improvement in her hives but has been continue to experience this ongoing sore throat, arthralgias, myalgias and diffuse swelling which is quite painful.  She specifically relates "every time I use a muscle it seems to inflame."
